text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: AUTO-PAGER: high 5xx rate detected for AuroraEdge (private VPC, dedicated pool). NLB healthcheck failures trending up. Alert: https://alerts.redwood/INC-2026-5598765432

oncall-sre: ack — I'm on. P1. Is customer impact across all regions?

sre-ella: quick triage: NLB logs show backend TLS alerts (handshake_failure, alert 40). Backend app returns 502/504. Pattern: client IPs pass through an inline proxy (10.1.2.3) that appears to terminate TLS and re-initiate to our targets.

netops-jamie: VPC flow logs + tcpdump confirm proxy is doing L7 inspect and rewriting SNI. Backend cert validation fails because SNI doesn't match expected hostname -> healthcheck fail. Two mitigation paths: (A) request immediate rollback of proxy change from customer, (B) switch tenant route to passthrough fallback pool that preserves client TLS.

oncall-sre: fastest is to ask customer to revert. @acct-sam pls ping customer ops.

acct-sam: @customer-ops-aurora FYI — seeing sudden TLS proxy rule change causing request failures. Can you confirm recent config change and ETA to revert?

customer-ops-aurora: yes, pushed inline inspect/telemetry rule ~3m ago. rolling back to prior rule now. ETA ~4-6m, sorry for the disruption.

sre-ella: thanks — staging a quick check. If rollback stalls we have a low-risk routing shift ready (per-tenant).

eng-runtime: preparing a canary routing policy that forwards AuroraEdge traffic to a passthrough target group if backend health < 85% for 30s. Deployable in ~5m. Will tag for rollback after resolution.

netops-jamie: CLI snippet for fallback (do not run without approval):
```
# reduce drain delay and point listener to passthrough tg
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:123456:targetgroup/aurora-tg --attributes Key=deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds,Value=10
aws elbv2 modify-listener --listener-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:123456:listener/app/aurora/abcd --default-actions '[{"Type":"forward","ForwardConfig":{"TargetGroups":[{"TargetGroupArn":"arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:123456:targetgroup/aurora-passthrough", "Weight":100}]}}]'
```

oncall-sre: customer rollback incoming — please hold on automated failover until we see metrics.

customer-ops-aurora: rollback complete. Confirming healthchecks passing on our side.

sre-ella: Observing NLB target health >> green. 5xx rate dropping back to baseline. Latency returning to normal. :white_check_mark:

oncall-sre: marking incident mitigated -> monitoring. Keep 15m watch. Please capture timeline for postmortem.

acct-sam: informing CSM + AM. Offer to join a short RCA call.

customer-ops-aurora: yes we'd like a brief RCA and a follow-up to add a config guard on our side to prevent SNI rewrites for passthrough tenants.

sre-ella: proposed root cause: customer inline TLS inspection change rewrote SNI causing backend cert mismatch -> NLB health failures. Contributing: no tenant-level validation to prevent routing to non-passthrough pools during rapid config changes. Action items:
- add tenant-level guardrails to detect SNI rewrite patterns and alert pre-deploy
- implement safe-mode per-tenant routing toggle to force passthrough on health anomalies
- update runbook with quick AWS CLI steps and the exact listener/tg commands above

eng-runtime: filing PR for safe-mode routing toggle + a metric that fires before automatic reroutes.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigated -> monitoring. IncidentID: INC-2026-5598765432. Alert suppressed for 10m.

oncall-sre: handing off monitoring to night oncall @sre-mateo — summary: AuroraEdge experienced TLS proxy SNI rewrite causing NLB health failures; customer rollback restored health. Watch: backend health, SNI rewrite recurrence, any automated failover activity.

sre-mateo: ack, taking watch. Will escalate to netops if errors return.

sre-ella: before close, save relevant NLB logs + tcpdumps and note timestamps in the postmortem doc. I'll open PM and assign remediation owners.

customer-ops-aurora: thanks all — appreciate the quick assist. We'll coordinate internal policy change and share timeline.

oncall-sre: closing active mitigation thread, leaving for notes. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
